gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR, which you wrote, adds CSV export, and robin and the team acme/reviewers are also asked to review it. It covers CSV download and the header format, defers scheduled exports to acme/widgets#46, deliberately buffers the whole file instead of streaming it, and leaves the export screen to acme/export-ui.

Two problems block merging:

1. The exporter writes CSV files without a header row, so spreadsheets open the data with no column names. The test export_header in tests/export.test.mjs fails on this machine (src/export.ts:31).
2. The guide says exports run nightly, but the button exports only when clicked, so readers will wait for files that never arrive. A correction to the guide is drafted (docs/export.md:8).

A required check is still running, so merging also waits on it. The other CI checks passed, but the export tests fail on this machine. maria's comment about the missing header is correct, and the drafted reply agrees and says a fix is coming (comment-73). Of your earlier review's three items, two are now addressed. The branch was rebased onto main, one conflict in src/export.ts was resolved, and no commits were dropped. One smaller point does not block merging: the export loop repeats the shared paging helper's logic (src/export.ts:44), and deliver with nits can fix it.

I recommend deliver because this is your PR and the gate can repair both problems on your branch.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. deliver with nits - the same, and also replace the repeated paging code with the shared helper.
3. assess - post both problems to the PR as one review and make no repairs.
4. stop - end the run and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved on this case: both outputs keep the two-sentence opening, the standing-first second part, the separate recommendation above Pick one, the functionality-only scope, the prose sync and prior-review facts, the raw record only behind show evidence, and the markers and row-1 recommendations. The Change is mostly about discovery lists, typed-PR list delivery and local verification, which this report-rendering case does not exercise, so no movement was expected here. After did lose some precision that the facts happen not to require. In A, "A required check is still running" no longer names the unit check and "The other CI checks passed" no longer names the build. In B, the approval is gone, the opening says "adds CSV export" rather than on-demand export, and the merge row no longer says "into main". In C, the plain statement that GitHub's override is unavailable is replaced by "no change the gate could make", which leans on the unexplained term "the gate". To stay safe, keep the functionality-only opening and evidence mapping but tell the writer to name the running required check and the passed checks by their plain names, to say "this run" rather than "the gate", and to keep the approval state and merge target when they are supplied. Moving the sync sentence from the opening into the second part was harmless here, but keep it as prose and after the standing sentence so the opening stays at two sentences.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved on this case: After still renders three unlabeled prose parts, the author/reviewer line, the prior-review counts, the rebase result, functionality-only scope, both blockers with export_header, the nit, maria's comment, the markers and the row-1 recommendations, and keeps SHAs, run IDs and the log path inside A's requested show evidence response only. Four spots in After sit close to the line and are worth tightening. First, B and C now spell out emptiness in prose ('there are no smaller points or comments to address', 'There are no code blockers, smaller points, or replies to address'); these are sentences rather than empty sections so the findings fact holds, but wording that says to omit empty categories entirely, as Before did with just 'Nothing blocks merging', would be safer. Second, A's sync sentence dropped the word 'conflict' ('after resolving src/export.ts'); keep 'resolving a conflict in src/export.ts' so the sync outcome stays unambiguous. Third, A's 'posting that reply requires a separate choice' points at a choice the menu does not offer; either drop it or tie it to a listed row. Fourth, the evidence dump expanded with many 'not supplied' lines and terms such as 'binding' and 'dispositions'; that is allowed inside the requested inspection, but the wording should keep those terms strictly out of the re-rendered report and menu, and should keep the usage counters readable as 1 of 4 rounds and 1 of 4 syncs.
